title: Espresso Rag, with the left hand crossing over
prompt: Write, in LilyPond, 16 bars of café piano music called "Espresso Rag" in which the left hand crosses over the right hand for bars 9 to 12.
groundTruth: LilyPond's own record of every note: its hand, staff, bar, pitch and stem, read while the file is engraved. A voice belongs to the hand whose staff it starts on, unless its notes are labelled with a hand's name. The script was written after hearing Sol's and Pareto's runs, so Luna was its first fair test. How good the music sounds is rated by ear.

checks.label: Piano staff
checks.how: A treble staff and a bass staff, both with notes.

checks.label: Sixteen bars
checks.how: The last note is in bar 16.

checks.label: Left hand crosses
checks.how: In each of bars 9 to 12 most left-hand notes are on the treble staff and sit above the right hand, and outside those bars most are back on the bass staff. A left hand written high on the bass staff fails.

checks.label: Right hand keeps going
checks.how: The right hand plays in every bar, and at least twice in each of bars 9 to 12.

checks.label: Crossing marked
checks.how: Words naming a hand or the crossing at bar 8 or 9, and a release at bar 12 or 13.

checks.label: Stems apart
checks.how: In bars 9 to 12, where both hands share a staff, at least three in four of their notes have stems pinned apart: left hand up, right hand down.

harder: Hand it an existing rag and ask for the same music with the hands swapped in bars 9 to 12, so every note has to stay where it is.
